name: Dark Mustard
lede: Dark Mustard is a deep, dull gold, a shade down from [[mustard]] and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a deep yellow.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No book in our library records a name at this position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark mustard" [1]. Its origin before that survey is undocumented here [1].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is deep yellow, under 3 CIEDE2000 units away, close enough that the two names describe much the same swatch, and the closest Munsell reading runs near 4.6Y in hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[brown-yellow]], [[mustard-brown]] and [[dark-goldenrod]], at 4.7, 5.7 and 5.8 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this swatch in 103 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. Its peak decade is the 1740s, at over six times the archive's baseline rate, and it is most common in works from India, the United Kingdom and the United States [2]. Paulus Potter's paintings carry it at 33 times the baseline, and it also turns up often in Rajput, Pahari and Mughal miniatures [2]. Where it appears, it is usually a highlight rather than a shadow, and the words "Olive" and "Khaki" share its canvases far more than chance [2].
